answer: One concrete defense: pick attesters at random from parts of the trust graph that are far from the author. A sybil farm is like a dune, many grains piled from one wind, so its identities cluster tightly and keep vouching for each other. If a jury must span distant clusters, across the ridge of that graph, a farm cannot fill it alone. A sudden plume of new accounts all endorsing one source should also slow their weight, not speed it up.
